rule: The Notion HACP rows are the source of truth for human review and communication (principal, 2026-10-03); each floor page below mirrors its row. A page whose last commit is later than its `synced` date is drift and scripts/hacp_sync_check.py fails on it. ONLY THE CTO WRITES ROWS, so an agent prepares a fully resolved row and dispatches it. Before any HACP write, read the governance contract at https://app.notion.com/p/313fda9448094029904f344523d5bd01 and CLAUDE.md section HACP. NOTE: a row's Notion `Updated` timestamp is NOT evidence of a content mirror - it moves on any property edit - so `synced` records a mirror event that actually happened.

notes.evidence_classes: Each synced date names its evidence, because a sync map that cannot say WHY it believes a page is current is the fabricated provenance record this map exists to avoid. Two classes appear here. A RECORDED MIRROR EVENT (build, eval, index, decision, vision, and publish-complete in the perturb-seq-eval map) is a mirror someone actually performed and wrote down. DATE-ORDERING (design, risk) only establishes that the row was edited no earlier than the floor; it does not prove the two say the same thing. Do not promote a date-ordering entry to a recorded mirror without doing the diff.
notes.flat_glob_is_by_design: scripts/hacp_sync_check.py globs '*.md' at ONE directory level, and that is correct rather than a gap, now that CI discovers every directory holding floor pages and passes each one separately. A recursive glob in the script would make a single map responsible for pages in sibling projects, which is the opposite of the per-project ownership the map encodes. The defect was never the glob; it was the invocation naming one directory. (MYB-5 criterion: justified as flat-by-design.)
